'''Microtech Knives, Inc.''' is a knife manufacturing company, famous for its [[automatic knife|automatic knives]],<ref name ="Walker"/> that was founded in [[Vero Beach, Florida]] in 1994, and operated there until relocating to [[Bradford, Pennsylvania]] in 2005 and to [[Fletcher, North Carolina]] in 2009. The company expanded the location of its Corporate Headquarters in nearby [[Mills River, NC]] in 2018. Microtech now has two active manufacturing factories and one corporate headquarters location.
[[File:MT-Hawk-Scarab.jpg|thumb|right|180px|a Microtech Hawk and OTF Scarab]]
The company has long promoted itself as stressing quality with regard to tight machining tolerances, to within one thousandth of an inch (0.001").<ref name ="Walker"/><ref>{{cite web  | title = Microtech Knives - About Microtech  | url = http://www.microtechknives.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=13&Itemid=30  | access-date = 2007-06-22
|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070213122820/http://www.microtechknives.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=13&Itemid=30 |archive-date = 2007-02-13}}</ref> Microtech has designed knives for use by the [[US Military]] such as the [[High-altitude military parachuting|HALO]], [[Underwater Demolition Team|UDT]], [[United States Special Operations Command|SOCOM]] and [[506th Infantry Regiment (United States)|Currahee]] models.<ref name="Walker"/><ref>{{Citation | date =  September 2007 | title = Microtech Knives: the Currahee | url = http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m3197/is_9_52/ai_n20512796
 | journal = Shooting Industry | access-date = 2008-02-06   }}</ref>  Custom knifemakers, such as Greg Lightfoot have remarked that these tolerances are what makes the factory knives so close to the custom design: "It has the same quality as a handmade custom."<ref name="Hopkins"/>

Although Microtech has produced many styles of blades in the past such as kitchen knives, fishing knives, [[arrow]] heads, and [[Butterfly knife|butterfly knives]]; Microtech is most famous for its tactical automatic knives.<ref name ="Rhea">{{Citation | last = Rhea  | first = David | year = 2005 | title = Butterfly Knives: Flippin' and Flyin' | journal = Blade Magazine | volume = 32 | issue = 9 | pages = 66–71}}</ref>   The most popular designs among collectors are the "[[OTF knife#Automatic OTF knives (switchblades)|Out The Front]]" ([[OTF Knife|OTF]]) and the "Double Action" (D/A) automatics.<ref name ="Karwan">{{Citation | last = Karwan  | first = Chuck
 | date = March 2005 | title = Microtech's X-Files: Fast & Furious | journal = Tactical Knives Magazine | volume = 11 | issue = 2 | pages = 10–14}}</ref>  Microtech along with [[Benchmade|Benchmade Knives]] was responsible for the resurgence in the popularity of tactical automatic knives in the 1990s.<ref name ="Karwan"/>  These knives were seen more as a precision made tool utilizing powerful springs and high grade bushings as opposed to a cheap import.<ref name ="Karwan"/>

Microtech has collaborated with famous knifemakers and designers such as [[Ernest Emerson]], [[Bob Terzuola]], [[Strider Knives|Mick Strider]], Walter Brend, Mike Turber, Greg Lightfoot, Reese Weiland, Borka Blades (Sebastijan Berenji) and Bastien Coves (Bastinelli Knives)  on exclusive designs.<ref name="Hopkins">{{Citation | last = Hopkins  | first = Cameron
 | date = September 2000 | title = These Hot Profit-Makers Are The Knife Industry's Best Kept Secret For Gun Dealers
 | url = http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m3197/is_9_45/ai_65953087 | journal = Shooting Industry | access-date = 2008-02-06}}</ref>  A Microtech Knives "HALO" was featured on the television series ''[[24 (TV series)|24]]''.<ref name ="Cerasini">{{Citation  | last1 = Cerasini  | first1 = Mark  | last2 = Alfonsi  | first2 = Alice  | year = 2003  | title = 24: The House Special Subcommittee's Findings at CTU  | pages = [https://archive.org/details/24housespecialsu00cera/page/224 224]  | publisher = [[Harper (publisher)|Harper]]  | isbn = 978-0-06-053550-6  | url-access = registration  | url = https://archive.org/details/24housespecialsu00cera/page/224  }}</ref>

Microtech Small Arms Research (MSAR) was a [[subsidiary]] of Microtech Knives which manufactured an American-made version of the [[Steyr AUG]] known as the MSAR [[STG-556]].<ref name ="Choat">{{Citation | last = Choat | first = Chris| date = March 2008 | title = Microtech's STG-556 An Exclusive First Look | journal = Small Arms Review | volume = 11 | issue = 6 | pages = 43–50}}</ref> Introduced at the 2007 [[SHOT Show]], the MSAR STG-556 is an AUG A1 clone available in either civilian, semi-automatic only and military/LE, select-fire variants. 

MSAR marketed accessories for its rifles until Microtech Knives Inc. closed down the division in March 2015.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.guns.com/news/2015/04/01/microtech-small-arms-says-farewell | title=Microtech Small Arms says farewell }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.thefirearmblog.com/blog/2015/03/23/microtech-small-arms-research-closes-its-doors/ | title=Microtech Small Arms Research Closes Its Doors - | date=23 March 2015 }}</ref>

Microtech Defense Industries is a current division of Microtech Knives exclusively manufacturing advanced firearm accessories. The first product launched was the R2K9 9mm Suppressor in 2019 and can actively be purchased through authorized dealers.
